content: Defibrotide should be administered intravenously at a dose of 25 mg/kg every 6 hours, infused over a period of 2 hours. The treatment should be continued for a minimum of 21 days. If signs and symptoms of hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD) have not resolved after 21 days, defibrotide therapy may be extended until VOD resolution or up to a maximum of 60 days. In cases of severe or life-threatening anaphylaxis, defibrotide must be permanently discontinued, and treatment should not be resumed. The dosage is based on the patient’s weight prior to the preparative regimen for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). Defibrotide increases the effects of alteplase, apixaban, argatroban, bivalirudin, dabigatran, dalteparin, desirudin, edoxaban, enoxaparin, fondaparinux, heparin, reteplase, rivaroxaban, tenecteplase, and vorapaxar through pharmacodynamic synergism. Co-administration of defibrotide with these antithrombotic or fibrinolytic drugs is contraindicated. This contraindication does not apply to the routine maintenance or reopening of central venous lines. Defibrotide may diminish the effects of thrombolytic agents when co-administered with aminocaproic acid, aprotinin, or tranexamic acid (oral or injectable) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended in such cases. Defibrotide enhances the effects of aspirin (oral and rectal), celecoxib, choline magnesium trisalicylate, citalopram, clopidogrel, diclofenac, diflunisal, escitalopram, etodolac, fenoprofen, fluoxetine, flurbiprofen, fluvoxamine, ibuprofen (oral and IV), indomethacin, ketoprofen, ketorolac (oral and intranasal), meclofenamate, mefenamic acid, meloxicam, nabumetone, naproxen, oxaprozin, paroxetine, piroxicam, prasugrel, salsalate, sertraline, sulindac, ticagrelor, ticlopidine, tirofiban, and tolmetin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter or other mechanisms. Caution and close monitoring are advised, as defibrotide may enhance the effects of platelet inhibitors. Fish oil triglycerides may increase the level or effect of defibrotide through anticoagulation. Prolonged bleeding has been reported in patients taking antiplatelet agents or anticoagulants alongside oral omega-3 fatty acids. Periodic monitoring of bleeding time is recommended in patients receiving fish oil triglycerides and concomitant antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapies. Ibrutinib may increase the level or effect of defibrotide through anticoagulation, potentially raising the risk of hemorrhage in patients receiving antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapies. Monitoring for signs of bleeding is essential. Defibrotide and warfarin may mutually enhance each other’s effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as defibrotide is contraindicated with systemic anticoagulants.
